pr_title: Increase ICMP timeout for PING sensor and device tracker
pr_body:

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
To respect slow devices being tracked, the ICMP time has been increased from 1s to 4s for `ping` `binary_sensor` and `device_tracker`.
In case you have set an own scan interval (_`interval_seconds`_) in the yaml configuration, you may need to increase the interval, to avoid overlapping of two scans in case of unreachable device.

issue_context.title: Standard ping timeout (1s) is too short
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Currently there is a timeout `ICMP_TIMEOUT = 1` set in [const.py](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/831c87205f2a06e2c2bf7172d6dd5d6d4087575b/homeassistant/components/ping/const.py#L13).

This might be way too short in some cases. In my case 4.9% of ping requests are slower than this (thank you internet monopoly in my street in Boston, USA). I still consider this to be reachable when it is within e.g. 2 seconds (1%), 3 seconds (0,4%) or even longer. Making this user definable would be nice.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Home Assistant 2022.9.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

ping

comments:
Hi @whnr 

this has been discussed with the HA core members. To make the ICMP timeout configurable would violate [ADR010](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0010-integration-configuration.md).
Therefore, we decided to just increase the timeout from 1s to 4s.
Great. 4s is a reasonable time in this world.

review_comments: Do we need to adjust the polling interval?
~~it's not the polling interval, but the timeout~~

ah, now i get it ... the polling interval is hard coded to 5min for the binary sensor and default 12s for the device trackers. So only in case for the device trackers when the user set an own interval in YAML (_key `interval_seconds`_), but this is not a documented (_but still an available_) option
anyway, in this case I would add a breaking change message, to inform the users, that the increased timeout may need an adjustment of their own scan interval settings
the `ping` command sends every 1s an ICMP echorequest (_Independent of given timeout value_)
